title: Building an AI Agent Loop - OpenClaw From Scratch (ep 1)
description:
In this series, I’m rebuilding a simplified version of OpenClaw to understand how it actually works under the hood. Plus it's a ton of fun!

In this first episode, we build the core agent loop from scratch in Python — about 150 lines of code across six files.

We start by asking the agent to:
"Write a Hello World Python script."
Then we execute it using a shell tool.
And it works.

That simple demo hides a powerful control system underneath.

*What You’ll Learn*
• The agent loop architecture (system prompt + history + user message → LLM → tool call → repeat)  
• Tool calling (read_file, write_file, exec)  
• How the loop decides when it’s done  
• Basic session storage using JSONL  
• A working interactive CLI agent  

This is the same core pattern used by Claude Code, OpenAI agents, and many other SDK-based systems — but here we build it ourselves to understand what’s really happening.

*GitHub Repo for code*
- https://github.com/jcdeichmann/rebuilding-openclaw-tutorial

*What’s Next*

In the next episode, we give the agent a personality.
We’ll add:
• soul.md  
• user files  
• a bootstrap flow  
So the agent can form an identity and remember who it is.

*Timestamps*
00:00 Demo – Agent writes and runs Hello World  
00:22 What is OpenClaw?  
01:54 Overview of today’s build  
02:40 The Agent Loop explained  
04:19 Code walkthrough (loop.py)  
08:09 Tools architecture  
11:07 Session storage (JSONL)  
12:00 Live CLI demo  
14:31 File system + session inspection  
15:15 What’s next (Personality)  

If you’re interested in building your own AI agents from first principles, this series is for you.
